transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you'd like to talk about?

Um, yeah… I guess I came in because I just feel wound up almost all the time. Like my body is bracing for the next bad thing, even when nothing is actually happening.

It’s weird because I can be sitting at my desk doing computer support stuff, just answering tickets, and I still feel like I’m tense, like I’m waiting for something to go wrong. Or even when I’m trying to enjoy dance night—which is supposed to be fun—I’ll notice I’m still kind of on edge. Like I can’t fully relax into it.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Yeah, definitely. It’s not even one thing anymore. At first I thought I was mostly stressed about the condo stuff, but now it jumps around constantly.

Like I’ll start wondering if my cousin is upset with me because she texted kind of short, and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether I’m going to mess up on a support call at work, and then it turns into this whole spiral about money and whether I’m ever going to save enough or move forward in my life. It’s like my brain just grabs onto whatever’s nearby.
Do you ever notice physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shaking when you're feeling this tension or worry?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I mean, I know I feel tense, like my shoulders are up by my ears a lot, but with the racing heart or sweating or shaking… I don’t know if I’ve really paid attention to that specifically.

Sometimes I get so in my head that I’m not even noticing my body, if that makes sense. Like I’ll be worrying about some tiny Slack message from work and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether my tone was weird, and then I’ve lost like twenty minutes. But as far as those specific things, I can’t say for sure.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that peaks within minutes, maybe with symptoms like shortness of breath, dizziness, or a feeling that you're detached from reality?

I’m not sure… I mean, I don’t think I’ve had something like that exactly, where it suddenly peaks in a few minutes. Or maybe I wouldn’t know what counts.

Like sometimes I’ll get really overwhelmed, but it’s usually more like my thoughts are piling up and I can’t get them to stop, not like a big wave out of nowhere. The detached-from-reality thing—I don’t know. I’ve definitely had moments where I’m kind of zoning out, like when I’m staring at my computer and realize I’ve reread the same ticket five times, but that might just be me being distracted.

So… I guess I’m not sure. I don’t have a clear example of that.
Have you ever had an episode where your heart raced, you felt shaky or sweaty, or you suddenly felt like you couldn’t breathe, even when there wasn’t an obvious reason for it?

I don’t think so… or at least I haven’t noticed it in that clear of a way.

Like, I get really caught up in my head and then later I’ll realize I’ve been sitting there completely tense, but I can’t say, “Oh yeah, my heart was racing” or “I couldn’t breathe.” I’m usually more focused on whatever thought I’m stuck on, like if I’m going to mess something up at work or if I said something weird to someone.

So I guess… no obvious episodes like that that I can point to. Or maybe I’m just not paying close enough attention to my body when it happens.
Have you noticed any episodes where you suddenly felt short of breath or dizzy, even when you weren’t doing anything physically strenuous?

I don’t think I’ve noticed that, no. Not suddenly, anyway.

I mean, sometimes if I’ve been sitting at my desk too long I feel kind of weird getting up, but that’s probably just because I forget to drink water or I’ve been hunched over for hours. My job is basically staring at tickets and messages all day, and then I realize I haven’t moved since lunch.

But in terms of suddenly being short of breath or dizzy when I’m just sitting there… I can’t really point to anything like that. I might be missing it, but nothing obvious comes to mind.
Have you ever had a sudden episode where you felt intense fear or discomfort that peaked within a few minutes, even if it only lasted a short time?

I don’t really have a clear “yes” for that. I keep trying to think of one, but nothing comes to mind where it was sudden and then peaked really fast.

I mean, I’ve had plenty of times where I’m uncomfortable or worked up, but it’s more like… it builds because I’m thinking about something, and then I get stuck on it. Like at work, if a ticket is vague and I’m worried I’m going to misunderstand it, I can kind of spiral, but that’s not really a few-minute episode, it’s more like I just keep chewing on it.

So I guess I’m not sure what would count, but I don’t think I’ve had that kind of sudden short burst.
Have you ever had a moment where you felt like you were having a panic attack — like everything was spinning out of control or you couldn't cope — even for a short time?

I’m not sure I’d call it that. I’ve definitely had moments where I feel like, “I can’t handle this,” but it’s usually tied to something specific I’m worrying about, and then I just keep going over it in my head.

Like, with work stuff, I can get really fixated on whether I answered something correctly, and then I’ll reread it too many times… actually, that reminds me, our ticket system has this annoying thing where it doesn’t show updates right away, so I’ll sit there refreshing it, which probably doesn’t help.

But, sorry, to answer your question—no, I don’t think I’ve had a moment that felt like a panic attack, exactly. Not like everything suddenly spun out of control for a short time. It’s more… drawn out, I guess.
Have you ever felt short of breath or dizzy while at rest, even if it wasn't sudden or very intense?

Not really, I don’t think so. I mean, “at rest” makes me think of just sitting on the couch or at my computer, and I can’t remember feeling short of breath or dizzy in a way that stood out.

Sometimes I’ll feel a little off if I’ve been sitting too long, but then I start wondering if it’s because I didn’t eat enough or I’ve been staring at screens forever. My desk setup is probably terrible too—I keep meaning to fix the chair height and then I forget.

But no, I don’t think I’ve noticed shortness of breath or dizziness just happening while I’m resting.
Do you find that your worrying happens more days than not, and that it’s hard for you to control or stop it once it starts?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not every single minute or anything, but more days than not, once something gets in my head it’s really hard to shut it off.

Like, I’ll tell myself, “You already checked the spreadsheet,” or “You already sent the email, it’s fine,” but then my brain doesn’t really accept that. It keeps looping back to it, and then one “what if” turns into a bunch of other ones. Like what if I missed a row, or what if the wording sounded wrong, or what if someone interprets it differently—and then I’m back checking again or just thinking about checking.

Sorry, I’m making it sound very work-specific, but that’s just where I notice it most because I’m at the computer all day. So… yes, it’s hard for me to control once it starts.
Would you say that you experience this tension or anxiety on most days, even when there’s no specific reason for it?

Yeah, I think that’s actually why I came in. I feel wound up almost all the time, like my body is sort of bracing for the next bad thing, even if nothing is happening.

Like I’ll just be sitting at my desk, doing normal stuff, and I’m tense for no clear reason. Or even when I’m trying to enjoy dance night—which is supposed to be fun—I still feel like I can’t fully relax. I’ll be there and part of me is still kind of… waiting for something to go wrong.
Have you noticed any other symptoms like feeling restless, having trouble sleeping, or feeling fatigued even when you haven’t been doing much?

Sleep, definitely. Most nights I get into bed already exhausted, like I’ve been waiting all day to finally lie down, and then my brain just… doesn’t stop.

I’ll start replaying loan notices or work tickets, or thinking about things I might have missed earlier. And then somehow it’s 2 or 3 in the morning, which makes me more stressed because I know I have to function the next day. I try not to look at the clock because that makes it worse, but then I do anyway.

And even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I barely rested. Like I was technically asleep, but not really recovered.
Do you often feel restless or like you can't settle down, even when you're not actively worrying about something?

Yeah, very much. Even when I’m not focused on one specific worry, I still feel kind of keyed up, like I can’t fully settle into my own body.

It’s like… I’ll just be sitting at my desk, nothing dramatic happening, and my shoulders are up and I’m bracing like something is about to happen. Or I’ll go to dance night, which I actually really like, and everyone’s having fun and I’m trying to enjoy it, but there’s still this part of me that feels wound up, like I’m waiting for the next thing to go wrong.

Sorry, that kind of loops back to what I said earlier, but yes — I feel restless or tense a lot, even when I can’t point to an exact reason.
Have you noticed that your muscle tension or physical restlessness occurs on most days, rather than just occasionally?

Yeah… it’s most days. I mean, that’s kind of what pushed me to come in, because it’s not like it only happens before a big meeting or something obvious.

I’ll just be sitting at my desk doing normal computer support stuff, and my whole body feels wound up, like I’m bracing for something bad to happen. And even on dance night — which is supposed to be fun, and I do like it — I still notice I’m tense and can’t fully let go.

So yeah, it’s more like a regular background thing than just occasional.
